name: Uduma ILC pilot in Mali – Option value CEA [February 2025]
summary: Pilots in-line chlorination of piped water in Mali, ahead of possible scale-up. GiveWell's spreadsheet "Uduma ILC pilot in Mali – Option value CEA [February 2025]", linked from its grant page. Every number is traced from the sheet's bottom line; calculated rows reproduce the sheet's own values.

Linked to the shared discount rate; GiveWell's sheet uses 0.04.

rows.label: How long we would fund program if we found it to be above our bar after the pilot (years) (8x bar for future opportunities)
rows.explainer: Assumption We benchmark this to the value typically used in other value of information/option value CEAs, but we have not explored this in-depth.

rows.label: Probability that we decide to scale up Uduma's program after the pilot (assuming no failure) (8x bar for future opportunities)
rows.explainer: GW Estimate This is a rough estimate of the probability that we will choose to fund a scale-up of Uduma's program if the pilot is successful. These are fairly high assumptions (40% to 65% depending on our bar at the time) because we currently estimate that Uduma's program in Mali and Burkina Faso would be above our bar. Therefore, we believe the most likely barrier to scale-up will be pilot failure.

rows.label: Probability the pilot fails (8x bar for future opportunities)
rows.explainer: GW Estimate Rough assumption that the pilot will fail, e.g. because Uduma's infrastructure isn't suitable for in-line chlorination (ILC) at reasonable cost, or because of security risks. A high assumption is used here (compared to GiveWell's default of 10%) because (1) experts have told us ILC is technically very challenging to install because of variations in the underlying water infrastructure (more here), and (2) Mali has security risks.

rows.label: Overall probability that we decide to scale up Uduma's program after the pilot (8x bar for future opportunities)

rows.explainer:
Calculated in the source sheet as `=IFERROR(__xludf.DUMMYFUNCTION("SUM(IMPORTRANGE(""https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1aFQ8FqBV2TH34lLGqcelBTrLuJVsHg63gH9LgYB2r4M/edit?gid=1988241019#gid=1988241019"", ""Uduma costs!D9"")+IMPORTRANGE(""https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1aFQ8FqBV2TH34lLGqcelBTrLuJVsHg63gH9LgYB2r"&"4M/edit?gid=1988241019#gid=1988241019"", ""Uduma costs!E9""))/1000000/10"),0.4361595104397531)`; kept as a fixed number here (operator &).

Calculation This is based on our estimates of room for more funding for Uduma's program in Mali and Burkina Faso over a 10 year window, which are then annualized here dividing them by 10. We consider these two countries only because we model Uduma's program in Côte d'Ivoire as well below our cost-effectiveness bar for funding. Note that these numbers include costs incurred by GiveWell only, not funds that we estimate are leveraged by our funding. See the calculations in our main cost-effectiveness analysis here.

Note also that this excludes the potential for expansion in Togo, Guinea, and Uganda, as planned by Uduma, since we haven't modeled the programs there and don't know whether they'd exceed our bar. This potential is accounted for separately through a rough supplemental adjustment below.

Risk that we learn this is above/below our bar and are wrong
rows.explainer: Assumption This captures the risk that we make a scale-up decision as a result of this pilot but were wrong to do so, e.g. because our cost-effectiveness analysis was wrong in some way.

rows.label: Risk that pilot/study is funded without us in a few years
rows.explainer: Assumption I use a low (-5%) adjustment here because we're already separately accounting for the likelihood that another funder will fund Uduma's chlorination costs in the "Leverage/funging" section of our main cost-effectiveness analysis. I think of this adjustment as specifically referring to the likelihood another funder would fund a similar operational pilot.

rows.label: Benefit from influencing other funders/value to broader research community
rows.explainer:
Assumption This parameter captures the idea that the trial we fund could update the funding decisions of other grantmakers/policymakers as well as our own. I think it's plausible that there could be demonstration benefits from showing other water utilities and funders that they could also chlorinate the water they deliver. 

I use a slightly lower assumption than GiveWell's default of 20%, because I'd guess RCTs are more likely to have benefits for the broader research community than operational pilots like this one, where the learnings might be more organization-specific.

rows.label: Adjustment to account for possible additional room for more funding in Togo, Guinea, and Uganda
rows.explainer:
GW Estimate Uduma expects to expand to new countries (Togo, Guinea, Uganda) in the future. The potential room for more funding from this expansion is not accounted for in our estimates of potential room for more funding above, which only consider Burkina Faso and Mali (not Côte d'Ivoire, where we estimate the program would be below our cost-effectiveness bar for funding). 

I roughly account for this with a +25% adjustment. This is relatively modest because I think all 3 countries where Uduma is considering expansion are likely to be less cost-effective than Burkina Faso and Mali, which we estimate are 2 of the highest-impact locations for chlorination programs based on rates of under 5-mortality and % of mortality from enteric infections (for more details, see cell note).

rows.label: Adjustment to account for direct benefits during the pilot
rows.explainer: GW Estimate This is a rough estimate of the benefits of the pilot itself. I assume these will be small because the pilot will be on 10 systems only, for 15 months, and focused on learning.

rows.label: Adjustment to account for generalizability
rows.explainer: GW Estimate The pilot we are planning to fund is likely to take place in one country (Mali), whereas scale-up is likely to happen in two (Mali and Bukina Faso). It's possible that this means we're overestimating the value of the pilot, either because the lessons won't usefully generalize to another context, or because we will need to fund another pilot before scale-up in country 2. This rough adjustment attempts to account for this.

rows.label: Total supplemental adjustment
Cost-effectiveness after all adjustments (x cash)
Units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for programs that mostly buy and hand out goods (nets, drugs, supplements, vaccines, water treatment): staff pay is a small part of the cost. Our judgment; we haven't seen this program's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Delivery staff are mostly hired locally at local rates, so the gap is small. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
